leads.title: ILGA-Europe Rainbow Europe Ranking 2023
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights ranking documenting Denmark as 3rd most LGBTQ-supportive country in Europe in 2023.
leads.detail: Cited in lead: 'In 2023, ILGA-Europe ranked Denmark as the third most LGBTQ-supportive country in Europe.' No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Lov om forbud mod forskelsbehandling på arbejdsmarkedet (Act on Prohibition of Unequal Treatment in the Labour Market)
leads.documents: Primary law prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation in employment; basis for later inclusion of gender identity/expression.
leads.detail: Cited as adopted in 1996 with definition quote: 'discrimination means any direct or indirect discrimination based on race, color, religion, political opinion, sexual orientation or national, social or ethnic origin.' No URL visible.

leads.title: 2015 Danish court ruling on transgender employment discrimination
leads.documents: Court ruling holding that gender identity or expression is included in the 1996 Act, in case of transgender woman suing former employer for alleged discrimination.
leads.detail: Cited as 'a 2015 court ruling, in which a transgender woman filed suit against her former employer.' No case number or URL visible.

leads.title: Lov om Ligebehandlingsnævnet (Act on the Board of Equal Treatment), 2008
leads.documents: Primary law establishing the Board of Equal Treatment to consider complaints of differential treatment including on grounds of sexual orientation.
leads.detail: Cited as passed in 2008 with mandate quote covering gender, race, colour, religion or belief, political opinion, sexual orientation, age, disability, etc. No URL visible.

leads.title: Danish Penal Code amendments 2004 - hate crime legislation
leads.documents: Criminal law providing additional penalties for crimes committed against people because of their sexual orientation.
leads.detail: Cited as 'amendments to the Penal Code in 2004, which provides additional penalties for crimes committed against people because of their sexual orientation.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Lov om sterilisation og kastration (Act on Sterilisation and Castration), June 1929
leads.documents: Early legal framework for legal gender change in Denmark; context for Lili Elbe and Christine Jorgensen cases.
leads.detail: Cited as adopted June 1929, 'one of the first gender change laws in the world.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Danish Parliament legal gender recognition reform - vote June 2014, effective 1 September 2014
leads.documents: Legal gender recognition law removing requirement of mental disorder diagnosis and surgery with irreversible sterilization; self-determination for 18+ with 6-month reflection period.
leads.detail: Cited as Parliament voted 59-52 in June 2014; effective 1 September 2014 for Danes over 18. No URL visible.

leads.title: Danish Parliament decision to remove Gender Identity Disorder from National Board of Health list - decided 2016, effective 1 January 2017; WHO action June 2018
leads.documents: Depathologization: Denmark as second country after France (2010) to remove transgender identities from mental illness list; WHO replaced GID with gender incongruence as sexual health condition.
leads.detail: Cited as pending WHO decision, Denmark postponed then decided to remove GID; change effective 1 Jan 2017; WHO change June 2018. No URL visible.

leads.title: Danish national guidelines on transgender healthcare (2023)
leads.documents: Government/clinical guidance restricting access: puberty blockers at Tanner stage 2 or 3, investigative interviews, psychiatric evaluation, age 15 consent for hormones, 18 for surgery, wait times 11-16 months hormones and 4-6 years bottom surgery.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Danish guidelines published in 2023 recommend the use of puberty blockers... at either Tanner stage two or three.' No URL visible.

leads.title: February 2013 asylum grant to Guatemalan transgender woman - documented incident
leads.documents: First transgender asylum grant in Denmark for persecution; documents placement in men's facility, sexual assaults, initial refusal, reopening after proof of danger on return to Guatemala.
leads.detail: Cited as February 2013 case: 'first transgender person to be granted asylum in Denmark.' No outlet/URL visible in provided text.
